findings.headline: Audit Wales review of counter-fraud arrangements identified seven recommendations requiring implementation by March 2027
findings.detail: An external review by Audit Wales of the council's counter-fraud arrangements identified seven areas requiring improvement. All recommendations have been agreed by management for delivery by 31st March 2027 and are being progressed in 2026/27.
findings.matters: An external regulator identifying required improvements to fraud prevention and detection arrangements indicates systemic weaknesses that required formal remediation planning
findings.quote: The Audit Wales Review of Counter Fraud Arrangements Report has been issued with seven recommendations made. All have been agreed by management for delivery by 31st March 2027 and are being progressed in 2026/27.

findings.headline: Counter-fraud investigations overran budget by 60% due to higher than expected number and complexity of cases
findings.detail: The council completed 17 investigations into fraud, theft, malpractice and whistleblowing in 2025/26. Investigation allegations included overtime claimed for hours not worked, abuse of sick pay policy, and non-declaration of interest. The 60% budget overrun indicates control issues were significantly more extensive than anticipated.
findings.matters: A large unbudgeted workload for fraud investigations suggests systemic control weaknesses across the council that could lead to undetected losses or overspend
findings.figures: 60% budget overrun on counter-fraud audit days; 17 investigations completed
findings.quote: Actual audit days for this area exceeded budget by 60%. This was largely due to the number and complexity of investigations required within year.

findings.headline: Neighbourhood Services Overtime received a 'no assurance' audit opinion, the only one issued in 2025/26
findings.detail: The internal audit found no assurance on the effectiveness of controls in Neighbourhood Services Overtime. Investigation themes in 2025/26 included overtime being claimed and paid for hours not worked, which represents direct financial loss. Management has accepted recommendations for remediation and is required to present to the Governance and Audit Committee.
findings.matters: Payment of staff for hours not worked is a control failure that causes direct cash overspend and indicates weaknesses in time recording or supervisory approval in that service area
findings.figures: 1 'no assurance' outcome out of 51 total audit reports issued
findings.quote: The no assurance outcome related to Neighbourhood Services Overtime.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Audit Wales Audit of Accounts Report 2025-26 Final
findings.headline: £1.68m correction to property valuations after audit found incorrect floor areas, rent, and pupil numbers used in valuation calculations for buildings
findings.detail: Audit testing of Property, Plant and Equipment identified that several buildings had been valued using wrong data—incorrect floor areas, rent figures, or pupil numbers. The council amended its accounts to increase the value of 'Other Land and Buildings' by £1,678,339, with corresponding adjustments to revaluation reserves and the Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Statement.
findings.matters: Material errors in property valuations point to weaknesses in the council's asset valuation process or controls. Property holdings are a core part of the council's balance sheet and often relevant to borrowing decisions.
findings.figures: £1,678,339 correction to Property, Plant and Equipment; £1,635,000 adjustment to Revaluation Reserve; materiality threshold set at £6.912 million
findings.quote: Audit testing identified that the incorrect floor areas, rent or pupil numbers had been used in the valuation calculation for some buildings. As a result, the financial statements were amended to increase the value of "Other Land and Buildings" in Note 11 by £1,678,339.

findings.headline: No detailed plan for preventative counter-fraud work; resources and delivery timescale not specified
findings.detail: While the Internal Audit Plan allocates resources for preventative counter-fraud work, this allocation lacks detail. Without a specific plan detailing priorities, responsibilities, resources and delivery timetable, the council cannot assure preventative work will be completed or targeted at actual fraud risks.
findings.matters: Preventative counter-fraud activity needs to be targeted and resourced to be effective; resources may otherwise not address the highest-impact fraud risks.
findings.figures: Resources allocated within Internal Audit Plan but without detailed specification
findings.quote: Without a specific plan for preventative works that details the necessary resources and delivery timetable, the Council cannot be assured that counter-fraud preventative works will be completed.
